# PART 2 – The claim and its estimand {.darkslide background-color="rgba(0,0,0,0)"}

::: {.partlabel}
Part 2
:::

::: notes
In Part 1 you met five analysts who took on one claim and came back with answers more than sevenfold apart, even once each was converted properly, and this part explains why. It begins inside the paper, with what it claimed, what it fitted and what happened when three kinds of repetition were tried on it. It then turns the question around, since much of what is called variability in analysis turns out to be variability in the question, and analysts who seem to disagree about an answer are often answering different questions without noticing. We therefore build the two tools that let you say precisely which question you are asking, the estimand and the causal graph, and you use both in the hands-on that closes the part.
:::
